This would result in the vast majority of movements of animals, animal products, plants and plant products between Great Britain and the European Union being undertaken without the certificates or controls that are currently required by the rules. It will also remove many post-Brexit restrictions on the movement of food between Britain and the North, which retains its dual market access.
